traditions.p: Ancient; in use since about 1900 BC
traditions.d: Hair removal with a cooked sugar paste, known as sukkar or ḥalawa in the Middle East, ağda in Turkey and moum in Iran.
traditions.tech: Paste of sugar, lemon juice and water applied by hand or spatula and flicked off, or used with cloth strips
traditions.mat: sugar, lemon juice, water; historically honey
traditions.auth: True sugar paste is water-soluble and resin-free; many shop products add wax.

traditions.r: India and Iran; spread to Europe and North America
traditions.p: Traditional; in the West from the 1980s
traditions.d: Hair removal with a doubled, twisted cotton or polyester thread rolled over the skin, mostly for shaping eyebrows.
